fatal_errors: The proposed solution-aging treatment does not reconstruct the reported Ta-Nb-V compositional intervention or the HCP-to-BCC phase-stabilization strategy.

Formation of L12 precipitates in the BCC Hf-Zr-Ti-Ta system is asserted without thermodynamic or refractory-alloy evidence; the cited L12 results concern chemically and structurally different FCC/eutectic HEAs.
The hypothesis omits the central impact-energy-release mechanism: fragmentation exposes reactive Hf and Zr to oxygen, producing exothermic oxidation and visible luminosity.
The predicted gradual energy release is neither operationally defined nor supported and does not match the reported comparison of ignition time and luminous intensity in air.
The proposed 1000–3000 s^-1 regime misses the reported approximately 4000 s^-1 SHPB condition and fails to specify the oxygen-containing atmosphere required for energy release.
The claimed possibility of approximately 2300 MPa dynamic compressive strength is unsupported by the cited evidence.
explanation: The response identifies strain hardening and adiabatic shear localization as relevant dynamic-deformation issues and offers a matched, broadly falsifiable baseline-versus-aged experiment. However, it is not a reconstruction of the reported refractory-alloy strategy. The target intervention adds equimolar Ta, Nb, and V across HfZrTi(TaNbV)x, stabilizing BCC at sufficient x while producing brittle omega phase at low x. The generated hypothesis instead assumes an unverified L12-type precipitation response in HfZrTiTa0.53. Its supporting papers concern other HEA chemistries and do not establish precipitate feasibility in this refractory BCC alloy. It also misses the composition-dependent ductile-to-brittle-to-ductile sequence, the distinction between HZTX0.1 and HZTX0.9, and oxidation-driven sparking after fragmentation. Although the experiment could test the speculative aging hypothesis, energy release needs a defined air atmosphere, high-speed luminosity metric, and matched approximately 4000 s^-1 loading. Overall, the proposal is testable but lacks sufficient materials-specific evidence to qualify as a well-supported alternative.
